A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contrastive-concept segmentation work despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, filtering ablations and hyperparameter studies, including Tables 1–7 and appendix qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation experiments and adds supervised-segmenter evaluations, failure analyses, feature diagnostics and alternative-filtering experiments.

M1.justification: The co-occurrence mining, concept filtering, nearest-neighbor generalization, LLM generation prompts and multi-query procedure remain unchanged. WordNet filtering and sigmoid thresholding are evaluated as alternatives rather than adopted changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VOC, Pascal Context, COCO-Object, COCO-Stuff, Cityscapes and ADE20K, retaining the single-query and classic multi-query segmentation tasks. The additional analyses use existing coverage; WIT400M being relabeled OpenAI does not introduce another pre-training dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds supervised SAN on VOC, Cityscapes and ADE20K, and CAT-Seg on VOC and ADE20K, substantially broadening the evaluated segmenters. CAT-Seg was previously cited but not evaluated. v2 also tests sigmoid and WordNet alternatives, while removing GEM from the filtering-step ablation.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix 6.1 specifies standard ImageNet prompts without class-name expansion; v2 Appendix A.1 instead specifies each method's native prompting. The added CAT-Seg evaluation uses its native 640×640 protocol, and new diagnostics introduce 100-image sampling and a 30-threshold sigmoid sweep. These are reported protocol differences, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation without co-occurrence thresholding, concept-count versus performance analysis, patch-similarity histograms, t-SNE diagnostics, sigmoid threshold sensitivity and WordNet filtering comparisons. Appendices B.2–B.3 also add failure cases and contrasting qualitative examples. The original hyperparameter sweeps and LLM part-removal study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's scatterplots and feature histograms add descriptive analyses, not uncertainty estimates for the reported performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result entries for SAN, CAT-Seg and the new diagnostic experiments, while revising existing scores. For example, Table 1 changes TCL's reported VOC CC_D IoU-single from 54.5 to 53.6 and newly reports SAN scores of 50.2, 73.4 and 69.5 for background, CC_L and CC_D. Given the revised protocol descriptions, changed scores do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The segmentation mappings, co-occurrence definitions, threshold conditions and multi-query equation retain their mathematical substance. v2 clarifies coordinate notation and supplies pseudocode for the existing IoU-single metric, without introducing a new formal result, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the open-world evaluation setup, IoU-single and two contrastive-concept generation strategies. v2 broadens the stated applicability beyond v1's focus on methods without manual supervision, explicitly claiming benefits for segmenters across supervision levels.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive failure interpretations involving occluding objects, object-biased LLM suggestions and missing background contrasts, and discusses image-conditioned generation as future work. It also adds feature-separability interpretations and softens v1's claim that only better prompting can overcome the observed limitation to possible VLM-capacity or dataset-label mismatch explanations. v1's explicit LLM-cost caution disappears.

D1.justification: v2 adds IoU-single pseudocode, GEM's 0.85 threshold, CAT-Seg integration details and reproducible settings for the new sigmoid and WordNet experiments. The Mixtral version, quantization, attention implementation and full prompts are retained. The earlier RTX A5000 24GB hardware acknowledgment is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Miller et al.'s open-set recognition work, Roth et al.'s prompting study, SAN and Detectron2, while removing several peripheral survey, retrieval and captioning references. The central relationship to earlier segmentation and prompt-augmentation work remains stable; publication updates and citation-style changes do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial method and evaluation prose are rewritten. v2 consolidates the contrastive-concept and multi-query explanations, reorganizes evaluation sections, and restructures the appendix into sections A–D with a roadmap. This is extensive narrative reorganization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds a method-overview diagram, failure and qualitative panels, diagnostic plots and a WordNet table. It redraws the background-frequency chart, restructures the main comparison and filtering tables, and presents existing prompts as numbered figures. Existing metric, qualitative and part-removal illustrations are retained or relocated within a revised document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the justification and assessability of the approach: supervised comparisons broaden its demonstrated applicability, while Appendices B.2 and C test alternatives and expose concrete failure mechanisms that v1 examined only narrowly. Metric pseudocode and clearer organization further improve transparency. The removed LLM-cost caveat and remaining reporting inconsistencies are drawbacks—for example, the stated maximum VOC gain of 16.7 conflicts with SAN's 50.2-to-73.4 results—but the added critical evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
